questions.question: During a National Emergency, the term of Lok Sabha can be extended for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one year at a time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During a **National Emergency**, the **term of the Lok Sabha can be extended by a maximum of one year at a time** through a law passed by the Parliament.
 
• This extension **cannot go beyond six months after the emergency is lifted**.
 
• Such provisions ensure the continuation of the legislative body during times of national crisis, maintaining governance and legislative functions.
 
• **Article** **352** of the Indian Constitution allows the President to declare a National Emergency in case of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: In which of the following sports/games is the term 'bull's eye' used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shooting**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'bull's eye'** is primarily used in the sport of **shooting**.
 
• In shooting, a bull's eye refers to the center of a target and is the area that scores the highest points when hit.
 
• The term is also used in other target-based sports such as **archery and darts**, but it is most commonly associated with shooting.
 
• Achieving a bull's eye is often considered a mark of precision and skill in the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shooting** is a competitive sport involving tests of proficiency (**accuracy and speed**) using various types of guns such as firearms and airguns.
 
• It is one of the oldest sports and has been a part of the Olympic Games since the **first modern Olympics in 1896**.
 
• There are multiple disciplines within shooting sports, including rifle, pistol, and shotgun events.
 
• Safety is paramount in shooting sports, and participants must adhere to strict safety guidelines and regulations.

questions.question: Kalidasa was a famous poet in the court of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa** was a renowned classical Sanskrit writer, widely regarded as the greatest poet and dramatist in the Sanskrit language.
 
• He was one of the "**Nine Gems**" (Navaratnas) at the court of **Chandragupta II**, also known as Vikramaditya, who ruled over northern India during the Gupta Empire.
 
• The period of Chandragupta II's reign is often considered the **Golden Age of India**, marked by significant achievements in arts, literature, and science.
 
• Kalidasa's notable works include plays like **Shakuntala, Meghaduta, and Raghuvamsha**, which have had a profound impact on Indian culture and literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Gupta Empire** (320 to 550 CE) is known for its extensive achievements in the arts, architecture, sciences, religion, and philosophy, often referred to as the Golden Age of India.
 
• **Chandragupta II's reign (380–415 CE**) was marked by prosperity, stability, and cultural flourishing, which provided a conducive environment for scholars like Kalidasa to thrive.
 
• Kalidasa's works have been translated into various languages and continue to be studied and performed worldwide, reflecting their timeless appeal and literary brilliance.

questions.question: Which type of muscles do the uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smooth muscles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain **smooth muscles**.
 
• **Smooth muscles** are **involuntary, non-striated muscles** found in various internal organs.
 
• These muscles are responsible for various involuntary movements in the body such as the contraction of the uterus during childbirth, adjustment of the iris in response to light, and regulation of airflow in the bronchi.
 
• Unlike skeletal muscles, smooth muscles are not under conscious control and are regulated by the autonomic nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Striated muscles** include **skeletal muscles** that are under voluntary control and are characterized by their striped appearance.
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are attached to bones and help in body movements.
 
• **Cardiac muscles** are specialized **striated muscles found only in the heart**, responsible for pumping blood throughout the body.
 
• Smooth muscles are also found in the walls of blood vessels, digestive tract, and other hollow organs.

• Rabindranath Tagore was a renowned poet, writer, and philosopher, and he was the first non-European to win the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913**.
 
• Tagore's actions inspired many others in the Indian independence movement to resist British rule through non-violent means.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Jallianwala Bagh massacre** is one of the most tragic events in Indian history and played a crucial role in galvanizing the Indian independence movement.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore's protest was not only a personal act of defiance but also a symbolic gesture that underscored the need for India's self-determination and freedom from colonial oppression.
 
• Tagore's literary works, including his poetry, songs, and essays, continue to inspire generations and are celebrated worldwide for their profound impact on literature and human thought.
 
• In addition to his literary achievements, Tagore also founded the **Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan**, which became a center for cultural and educational exchange.

questions.question: Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam and Tillana are regular patterns of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• The dance form is known for its **fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions**.
 
• Regular patterns in Bharatanatyam include **Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, and Tillana**.
 
• These components form the structure of a traditional Bharatanatyam performance, each with its unique significance and role in storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alarippu** is an invocatory piece that **symbolizes the blossoming of a flower**.
 
• **Jatiswaram** combines intricate footwork with melodic patterns without any expressive elements.
 
• **Shabdam** incorporates expressive gestures and is usually a narrative piece.
 
• **Varnam** is the centerpiece of a **Bharatanatyam recital**, combining both expressive and technical aspects.
 
• **Tillana** is a lively and rhythmic conclusion piece, often highlighting the dancer's technical prowess.
 
• Bharatanatyam is deeply rooted in the spiritual and cultural traditions of India and often depicts themes from Hindu mythology.

questions.question: The Federal Court of India was established in Delhi by the Act of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1935**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Federal Court of India** was established in Delhi by the **Government of India Act**, **1935**.
 
• The court was inaugurated on **October 1, 1937**, and** functioned until January 28, 1950**, when the Supreme Court of India was established.
 
• The Federal Court had jurisdiction to resolve disputes between provinces and states and hear appeals against judgments from the High Courts.
 
• It played a crucial role in the interpretation of the Government of India Act, 1935, and laid down several important legal principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Government of India Act, 1935, was the last pre-independence constitution of India**, which provided for greater autonomy to Indian provinces.
 
• It also introduced direct elections, increased the franchise, and expanded the participation of Indians in governance.
 
• The act was instrumental in shaping the constitutional framework that eventually led to the formation of the Republic of India.
 
• The **Federal Court was succeeded by the Supreme Court of India**, which was established under the Constitution of India on January 28, 1950.
 
• The Supreme Court of India now serves as the highest judicial authority in the country, ensuring the rule of law and protecting the rights and liberties of citizens.

questions.question: The density of population is the crude relationship between human and ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**land**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Density of population** refers to the number of people living per unit area of **land**.
 
• This metric is important for understanding how populated an area is and can influence planning and resource allocation.
 
• It is **calculated by dividing the total population by the total land area**.
 
• **Higher population density** can indicate **urbanization**, while **lower population density **may be indicative of **rural areas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Population density is a crucial factor in **urban planning** and **development policies**.
 
• Regions with high population density may face challenges like **overcrowding, pollution, and strain on resources**.
 
• Conversely, areas with low population density might struggle with **underdevelopment and lack of services**.
 
• Understanding population density helps governments and organizations to plan for **infrastructure, healthcare, education, and other essential services**.
 
• Population density varies widely across different parts of the world and can be influenced by factors such as **geography, climate, and economic opportunities**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about the Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy has been taken from the Irish Republic.
They were incorporated in our Constitution in order to provide economic justice.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**these principles are justiciable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** is the correct answer because the **Directive Principles of State Policy are not justiciable**, meaning they are** not enforceable by any court**.
 
• The Directive Principles are **fundamental in the governance of the country** and aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The idea of Directive Principles of State Policy has indeed been **taken from the Irish Republic** and incorporated into the Indian Constitution.
 
• They were included in our Constitution to **provide economic justice** and to help achieve a welfare state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are listed in **Part IV **of the Indian Constitution from **Article 36 to Article 51**.
 
• They are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government and aim at ensuring **socio-economic justice**.
 
• Though they are non-justiciable, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and act as a yardstick in the making of laws.
 
• These principles reflect the ideals that the state should strive to achieve to promote the welfare of the people.
 
• Unlike the **Fundamental Rights, which are enforceable by the courts,** the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: Rajasthani architecture is also known as:

__
 
• **Maru-Gurjara** architecture, also known as **Rajasthani architecture**, is a style that emerged in the Indian state of Rajasthan and nearby regions.
 
• This architectural style is characterized by its intricate carvings, expansive courtyards, and ornate facades.
 
• Notable examples of **Maru-Gurjara architecture** include the forts, palaces, and temples of Rajasthan, such as the **Hawa Mahal in Jaipur and the Dilwara Temples on Mount Abu**.
 
• The style reflects the rich cultural heritage and artistic traditions of the region, blending elements from Hindu and Jain architectural principles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rajasthan's architecture is not just limited to Maru-Gurjara; it also encompasses Mughal and colonial influences seen in various structures across the state.
 
• The use of locally available materials like **sandstone and marble** is a significant aspect of Rajasthani architecture.
 
• Many of the structures built in this style are designed to withstand the harsh desert climate, featuring thick walls and small windows to keep interiors cool.
 
• Rajasthan's architectural heritage is a major attraction for tourists, contributing significantly to the state's economy.

questions.question: Identify a factor that does NOT determine the temperature of ocean waters.

options.text: Unequal distribution of land and water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Longitude**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Longitude** does not determine the temperature of ocean waters.
 
• The temperature of ocean waters is influenced by factors such as **unequal distribution of land and water, latitude, and ocean currents**.
 
• **Latitude** **affects temperature** as it determines the angle of the sun's rays and length of daylight.
 
• **Ocean currents** can** carry warm or cold water** across different parts of the ocean, affecting local temperatures.
 
• **Unequal distribution of land and water** influences the temperature due to different heat capacities of land and water bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Latitude** is a geographical coordinate that specifies the **north–south position** of a point on the Earth's surface.
 
• **Longitude** is a geographical coordinate that specifies the **east–west position** of a point on the Earth's surface but does not influence temperature.
 
• **Ocean currents** are continuous, directed movements of seawater generated by forces such as wind, temperature differences, and salinity gradients.
 
• The **unequal distribution of land and water** leads to varying heating and cooling rates, affecting the climate and temperature of adjacent ocean waters.

questions.question: Which metalloid in the carbon group is chemically similar to its group neighbours tin and silicon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Germanium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Germanium** is a metalloid in the **carbon group (Group 14)** of the periodic table.
 
• It shares similar chemical properties with its group neighbours, **tin and silicon**.
 
• Germanium has a similar electron configuration to tin and silicon, leading to comparable chemical behavior.
 
• It is used in semiconductors and various electronic applications, similar to silicon.
 
• Germanium forms compounds like germanium dioxide (GeO₂) and germanium tetrachloride (GeCl₄), which are analogous to silicon and tin compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Germanium** was discovered by **Clemens Winkler in 1886**.
 
• It is a **lustrous, hard, grayish-white metalloid in the carbon group**, chemically similar to its group neighbours tin and silicon.
 
• Germanium is less abundant in the Earth's crust compared to silicon but more abundant than tin.
 
• It is primarily obtained from **sphalerite **(zinc ore) and from the by-products of coal combustion.
 
• In addition to its use in electronics, germanium is also used in fiber optics, infrared optics, and as a catalyst in polymerization processes.

questions.question: Identify the Mughal emperor who was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra after the war of succession among his sons.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shah Jahan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shah Jahan** was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra after the war of succession among his sons.
 
• Shah Jahan was the** fifth Mughal emperor**, who reigned from **1628 to 1658**.
 
• He is best known for commissioning the construction of the Taj Mahal in Agra, in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• After a fierce war of succession among his sons, Shah Jahan was overthrown by his son Aurangzeb, who then imprisoned him in the Agra Fort.
 
• Shah Jahan spent the remaining years of his life in captivity, where he **died in 1666**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb** was the **sixth Mughal emperor** and ruled from **1658 until his death in 1707**.
 
• The Mughal Empire reached its **greatest territorial extent under Aurangzeb**, but his reign was also marked by increasing internal strife and rebellion.
 
• The Mughal Empire began to decline rapidly after Aurangzeb's death, leading to the eventual establishment of British colonial rule in India.
 
• The imprisonment of Shah Jahan by Aurangzeb is often seen as a pivotal moment in Mughal history, reflecting the intense power struggles within the royal family.

questions.question: What is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mitochondria** are known as the **powerhouse of the cell** because they generate most of the cell's supply of **adenosine triphosphate (ATP)**, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are **double-membraned organelles** found in most **eukaryotic cells**.
